Two p-n silicon diodes are connected in series as shown in <image 1>. A 5-V voltage is impressed upon them. Find the voltage across each junction at room temperature ($\eta V_T$ = 0.052 V). What is their absolute difference in terms of V?
explanation:
The current I is the same throughout a series circuit. Clearly, this

    current is in the forward direction through one diode and in the reverse
    
    direction through the second diode. Hence I = IO and the voltage V1 across
    
    the forward-biased junction can be found from the following equation:
    
                            I = IO(e[{(V)1} / {\eta(V)T}] - 1) = Io
    Dividing by IO we can obtain

                            e[{(V)1} / {\eta(V)T}] = 2
    
    Taking the natural logarithm of both sides of the equation,
    
                            [(V1) / (\etaVT)] = 0.693
    
    V1 = 0.036 V
    
    The voltage V2 across the reverse-biased diode is V2 = 5 - 0.036 = 4.964
    
    V. Note that only a small voltage is needed across the forward-biased
    
    junction to produce the small current Io and that almost all of the applied
    
    voltage appears across the reverse-biased diode.

In the emitter-bias circuit shown in <image 1>, $R_C$ = 10 k$\Omega$, $R_E$ = 1 k$\Omega$, and $V_{CC}$ = 20 V. Given that $\beta _O$ = 80 and $V_{BE}$ = 0.6 V, find R1 (k$\Omega$) to set $V_{CQ}$ at the center of the active region.
explanation:
We will first assume that R2 = 10RE is a condition imposed on the

                        circuit by stability requirements. This gives a value of R2 = 10 k\Omega for this

                        example. We now must find the desired value of IBQ.

                        The center of the active region must be located. The center lies halfway

                        between the maximum and minimum values of VC. The maximum value

                        occurs when IC = 0, VC = VCC. The minimum value occurs when the

                        transistor saturates. It then acts as a short (VCE(sat) << VCC), so by voltage

                        division

                                    VC = [RE / (RC + RE)]VCC

                        The halfway point is then

                                    VCQ = (1 / 2) (VCmax + VCmin) = (VCC / 2){1 + [RE / (RC + RE)]}

                                    VCQ = 10{1 + (1 / 11)} = 10.9 V.

                        The required collector current and base current can now be found to give

                        this value of VCQ:

                                    VCQ = [(VCC - VCQ) / RC] = [(20 - 10.9) / 10 k\Omega] = 0.91 mA,

                                    IBQ = (ICQ / \betao) = (0.91 / 80) 0.0114 mA.

                        We now select R1 to give the calculated value of IBQ. By noting in the

                        figure that I1 = IBQ + I2, we can find the necessary value of R1:

                                I2 = (VBQ / R2) = [(IEQRE + VBE) / R2] = [{(IBQ + ICQ)RE + 0.6} / R2]

                                    = [{(0.92)1 k\Omega + 0.6} / 10 k\Omega] = 0.152 mA;

                                I1  = IBQ + I2 = 0.011 + 0.152 = 0.163 mA:

                        Since the voltage across R1 is VCC - VBQ, then

                                    R1 = [(VCC - VBQ) / I1] = [(20 - 1.52) / 0.163] = 113 k\Omega.

Find: Whether the MOSFETs operate within safe limits.
explanation:
In the stable state, Q2 is on and Q1 is off. The gate of Q2 draws

                        no current, and there is no drain current in Q1, so VGS2 = VGS1 = VDD.

                        There is no input at the trigger, so VGS1 = 0.

                        A pulse at the trigger turns Q1 on. This causes VDS1 to go low, and C

                        transmits the drop to the gate of Q2, turning it off, and forcing VDS2 to go

                        high. C begins charging. When VDS1 + VC = VTH, Q2 goes on, VDS2 goes

                        low , Q1 shuts off, C discharges, and the circuit goes back into its stable

                        state.

                        When a MOSFET in this circuit is on, the current through it is

                                             ID (ON)   = {(VDD) / (RD + RDS(ON))}

                                                            = {(12) / (2k\Omega + 100)}

                                                            = 5.714 mA

                        ID , VDD , VGS are all below their respective maximum\xadrated values.

                        Therefore, the MOSFETs operate within safe limits.

                                                Eo(max) = 20 V + 1 V = 21 V

                        Using

                                                sin \theta1 = [{Eo(min)} / {Eo(max)}]

                                                sin \theta1 = (19 / 21) = 0.905                 or         \theta1 = 65°

                                    The period of the input wave is the reciprocal of the frequency,

                                                T = (1 / 60) = 16.6 ms.

                                    This T is the time for a complete cycle or 360°.

                                                ICQVCEQ = PC,max                                                                     (3)

question: The given figure <image 1> shows the model of a CE amplifier. Find the current gain if hre = 10-4 and hoe = 10-4 mho.
explanation:
Referring to the output circuit, using current division,

                                                iL = (- 50)[(2.75) / (2.75 + 1)]ib = -36.7ib                            (1)

                                    Note that

                                                vce = iL * 1k\Omega

                        or

                                                vce = - 36.7 * 103ib                                                               (2)

                        Turning to the input circuit and applying KVL,

                                                vb = (0.83k\Omega)ib - 10-4Vce

                   Using eq. 2 to substitute for Vce, we get

                                           vb  = 830ib - (10-4)(36.7 * 103)ib

                                                = (830 - 3.67)ib \approx 830ib

                        The effect of hre is therefore negligible in this (and most) examples.

                                    The current gain is

                                                Ai = (iL / ii) (ib / vb) (vb / ii)

                        where

                                                (iL / ib) = - 36.7          (ib / vb) = (1 / 830)

                        and using KCL at the base,

                                            ii   = vb[(1 / 10k\Omega) + {1 / (8.3kk\Omega)}] + ib

                                                \approx vb[(1 / 10k\Omega) + {1 / (8.3k\Omega)} + {1 / (830\Omega)}]

                                                = (vb / 700)

                        Thus

                                                Ai \approx (- 36.7)(1 / 830)(700) = - 31

                        The effect of hoe is to reduce the gain. This small reduction in gain is

                        usually insignificant.
